question.prompt: Ms. Blackwell gives an exam to two classes. The mean of the scores of the students in the morning class is \(84,\) and the afternoon class’s mean score is \(70.\) The ratio of the number of students in the morning class to the number of students in the afternoon class is \(\frac{3}{4}.\) What is the mean of the scores of all the students?

solutions.title: Combine the score totals
solutions.explanation:
The classes have different sizes, so their means must be weighted by their student counts. We can do this by recovering each class's total score.

Write the morning and afternoon class sizes as \(3k\) and \(4k\), respectively, where \(k>0\). Since a mean is the total score divided by the number of students, the two score totals are
\[
84(3k)=252k
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
70(4k)=280k.
\]
Together, the \(7k\) students have a total score of \(252k+280k=532k\). Their mean is therefore
\[
\frac{532k}{7k}=\frac{532}{7}=\boxed{76}.
\]
The answer is \(\textbf{C}\).
